about: Escape Animals sends you out from a base to find blocky animals. The open area contains hazards such as bursts of lava and terrain traps. Look for a return route before moving toward an animal, especially when the nearest path narrows.
Collecting an animal is the first half of a trip. Bring it back to the base to secure the reward. A close animal can be a good early choice when you can reach it and return through open ground.

Animals have different rarities and variants, and base upgrades affect the income they produce. Use earnings from successful short trips to improve your collection before attempting a route with more difficult obstacles.
steps: Move and check the camera
Use WASD or the arrow keys to move. Use the right mouse button to adjust the view and check the route back.
Collect an animal with E
Get close and press E. Turn toward the base once you have the animal and watch for changes along the return path.
Clear or avoid an obstacle
Use the left mouse button for the game's attack or obstacle action. Look for an open route when stopping would put the pickup at risk.
Upgrade at the base
Use F at the base to upgrade animals. Compare the cost and income from your current collection before choosing the next trip.
faq: When is an animal secured?
Return safely to the base after collecting it. The completed trip is what lets the animal contribute to your income.
Which key picks up an animal?
Press E when you are close enough to the animal.
How do I improve income at the base?
Bring back animals and use F to upgrade them at the base. Rarity and upgrades affect the value of your collection.

en.summary: Choose a class and clear dungeon waves in Stick Hero RPG. Use movement, skills and earned gold to build a character for harder encounters.
en.aboutTitle: Build around the class you want to play
about: Your first choices in Stick Hero RPG are a species and a class. Humans, elves and orcs offer different starting styles. The Gunner, Wizard, Archer and Thief classes give you different ways to attack and spend skill points.

Dungeon stages play out from the side. You move, jump and use attacks while keeping track of health and mana. Early waves are a chance to learn your class's reach and ability timing before a boss arrives.

Gold earned from battles pays for equipment and upgrades. If you are consistently running out of health before a wave ends, improve survival first. Once you can finish a wave reliably, invest in the damage or abilities you use most.
steps: Pick a species and class
Choose from the starting options. Learn one class's basic movement and attacks before comparing another.
Move and jump through the stage
Use A and D or the left and right arrows to move. Press Space, W or the up arrow to jump.
Aim attacks and use skills
Hold the left mouse button and move the pointer to aim your in-game attack. Use the number keys for equipped skills.
Set a priority for earned gold
When a stage ends, compare upgrades against the part of the encounter that gave you trouble. Spend toward one goal and try another wave.
faq: Which keys trigger skills?
Use the number keys assigned to your skills. Check your current abilities before entering the next wave.
Can I restart the current round?
The published controls assign E to reset the round.
How should I spend early skill points?
Start with abilities that support the class you actually use in fights. Monitor health and mana before deciding whether to invest in survival or damage.

en.summary: Slide and merge evolving creature tiles in 2048 Rogue. Leave room for new tiles and choose between a story route and endless play.
en.aboutTitle: Leave a route for the next matching tile
about: Each arrow input moves the board in one direction. Identical icons combine into a higher form, and a new tile can appear after a move. Look at the whole board before sliding, since a useful merge can also shift pieces you were saving.

A corner gives you a place to build a high-tier creature while lower forms line up beside it. Read the rows that feed that corner. If a slide separates two matching icons, check whether another direction keeps them together.

Story mode adds structured objectives and narrative fragments. Endless mode lets you focus on keeping the board playable. Undo can help you review a move that closed an important gap. Check how the board changes before repeating the slide.
steps: Slide with the arrow keys
Choose a direction and watch all tiles move together. Matching icons can merge into a higher form.
Keep a space beside a developed tile
Try building toward one edge so you can feed that tile from a neighboring row. Check which other lines will shift first.
Check what a move does to the board
Before sliding into a near-full side, look for at least one merge or opening to use on the following move.
Review a close call with Undo
Use Undo when available to revisit a slide that separated a pair or trapped several tiles. Compare another direction before committing.
faq: What ends a run?
The run ends when you have no legal moves left.
What do matching tiles turn into?
Two identical icons merge into a higher form. The game uses evolving creatures and objects as its tiles.
How do Story and Endless differ?
Story adds objectives and narrative fragments as you advance. Endless emphasizes keeping the board open and merging for longer.

en.summary: Switch lanes with one click in Tap Road. Dodge numbered blocks as the neon road speeds up and collect spheres to unlock tracks and ball designs.
en.aboutTitle: Watch the next pair of blocks instead of the ball
about: The ball rolls forward automatically along two lanes. Click to move it to the opposite lane before it reaches a numbered block. You score by dodging obstacles, and the road gets faster during the run.

Look beyond the nearest block to see which lane the one after it occupies. Changing lanes too early can put you in the path of a closer obstacle. Changing back immediately can leave you with too little time for the next move.

Spheres can buy tracks and ball designs, while challenges offer additional rewards. Take a sphere when the approach and exit are clear. A clean run gives you more chances to see how the obstacle pattern changes at higher speeds.
steps: Click to switch lanes
One mouse click sends the ball into the other lane. Wait until the next action actually needs a lane change.
Look two blocks ahead
Identify which lane holds the nearer block. Then check whether you will need to switch back for the following one.
Take spheres on a clear route
Collect spheres when they are along the lane you can hold safely. Skip ones that would put you in the path of a numbered block.
Use challenges to pick a goal
Check the listed challenges between runs. Focus on a single goal while you practice changes at higher speeds.
faq: Can I slow down the ball?
The ball moves forward and speeds up automatically. Your control switches it between the two lanes.
How is the score counted?
Your score reflects how many obstacles you dodge. Spheres are a separate pickup.
What can I buy with spheres?
Use collected spheres toward more tracks and ball designs.

en.summary: Build power, rotate and land on your feet in Flip Rush. Practice the release timing across parkour courses with different takeoff points.
en.aboutTitle: Release the rotation with the landing zone in view
about: Flip Rush asks you to land on your feet inside a marked area. Hold the left mouse button or Space to build power and rotate. Release as you approach the position you need for the landing.
The opening tutorial walks you through the motion. Use it to see how long a short rotation takes. On later layouts, check the height and position of the next target before deciding how long to hold.

Finishing a location's levels opens the next setting. A takeoff that works in the gym may leave you rotating too late on a mountain or city stage. Start with a clean landing before trying to earn more points from another rotation.
steps: Learn the hold and release in the tutorial
Hold left-click or Space to build the movement, then release to prepare for landing.
Read where the target begins
Check whether the landing zone is close below you or farther away. Use that distance to judge when you should stop rotating.
Correct one part after a missed attempt
If you reach the area while still turning, try releasing sooner. If you fall short of the area, compare the next takeoff without changing everything at once.
Complete a location to advance
Finish the stages in the current setting to open the next. Learn the first landing there before attempting longer combinations.
faq: Can I use Space instead of the mouse?
Yes. Holding Space or the left mouse button builds power and rotation. Release to set up your landing.
What counts as a clean landing?
Finish on your feet inside the marked target zone. An awkward landing can lower the score or fail the attempt.
How do I open another location?
Complete the stages in the current location. The next setting then becomes available.

en.summary: Ride a sled through changing winter courses in Slope Rider 3D. Jump past logs and gaps, collect gift boxes and try Normal or Hard mode.
en.aboutTitle: Set up the next turn before you leave the snow
about: Slope Rider 3D sends you down a changing winter course. Rolling logs, falling trees and snow boulders can block space you planned to use. Read where the obstacle will be when you arrive, especially if you need to jump.

Normal and Hard modes let you choose the challenge. Use Normal to learn how long your sled stays in the air and how quickly it can steer after landing. Try Hard once you can set up the turn after a jump without swinging across the whole track.

Gift boxes unlock sleds with different performance traits. A quicker sled can give you less time between nearby obstacles. Try a new sled over a few clear descents to get used to its steering and jump timing.
steps: Steer left or right
Use the arrow keys to guide the sled. Make a clear move before the path narrows.
Jump with the up arrow or Space
Use either key to clear a log or gap. Look for a clear landing strip before leaving the snow.
Pick up gifts when you can exit safely
Follow a gift line when there is room after it for your next turn. Leave a box behind if it is beside a moving hazard.
Compare Normal and Hard
Practice judging the distance to a log on Normal. Use the same look-ahead habit when you try Hard.
faq: Is the course identical on every descent?
No. The game changes the terrain and obstacle placement, so watch the current slope instead of memorizing a single route.
What can I use gift boxes for?
Collected gifts can unlock additional sleds with different handling, jumping or speed traits.
How can I jump and steer with separate controls?
Use the left and right arrows to steer and Space to jump. The up arrow also jumps.

en.summary: Collect Brainrots and get back to base before waves sweep the course. Use trenches for shelter and upgrade your speed, carrying capacity and base.
en.aboutTitle: Pick a return route with a trench in reach
about: Brainrots appear on platforms along the course. Collect one and bring it back to base to start earning income from it. A farther platform can offer a more valuable pickup, but it also leaves a longer trip back.

A tsunami can sweep the course while you are out collecting. Trenches give you a place to wait for it to pass. Before heading farther out, look for a trench you can reach from the platform you are aiming for.
Income from returned units pays for improvements. Speed helps when the trip itself takes too long. Capacity lets you carry more in one outing, while extra slots give you room for more units at base.
steps: Set out and check the route
Move with WASD or the arrow keys. Use the right mouse button to adjust the camera so you can see the platforms and nearby trenches.
Pick up a Brainrot
Press E when you are close enough to a unit. Use Space to jump over gaps in the course and check your landing before leaving the platform.
Get out of the wave's path
If a wave approaches and the base is too far away, aim for a trench and wait for the wave to pass before continuing.
Use the income to improve the next trip
Return the Brainrot to base. Consider a speed upgrade if travel time keeps cutting your trips short, or capacity if you often leave reachable units behind.
faq: Where can I wait for a wave to pass?
The trenches along the running track serve as safe zones. Look for one before you head into a distant section.
When do Brainrots start earning income?
Bring them back and place them at your base. Units still on the course do not contribute to the base.
What can I upgrade between trips?
The game lets you improve movement speed, carrying capacity and the number of available base slots.

en.summary: Time a cannon launch in Ragdoll Launcher. Guide the ragdoll through the air, use boosts and earn upgrades for longer runs.
en.aboutTitle: Judge the launch and first bounce separately
about: A moving cannon and a power indicator determine the start of the run. Watch the aim and release timing before clicking. A strong launch still needs an angle that carries the character into an open part of the course.

You can drag the mouse to make small adjustments once the ragdoll is airborne. A trampoline or another in-game boost can keep the flight going. Scan for a clean way through before making a large adjustment toward one.

Distance earns rewards that help unlock improvements. Watch the first landing on early attempts. If you lose momentum immediately, compare a different launch timing before changing the upgrade you are saving for.
steps: Watch the indicator before clicking
Wait until the cannon points toward a clear route and the power indicator is near the part of its range you want.
Make a small correction in the air
Drag the mouse to guide the ragdoll. Let the movement settle before making another change.
Look for a reachable boost
Use a trampoline or other boost when it is near the flight path. Keep a clear route through the next set of obstacles.
Compare two launches
Try similar power with a slightly different aim. See which one reaches a better first bounce before investing in another upgrade.
faq: Which control launches the ragdoll?
Click when the cannon and power indicator are where you want them.
Can I adjust direction after launch?
Yes. Drag the mouse in the air to guide the character toward a landing or boost.
Why do runs with similar power end at different distances?
Launch angle, bounces and obstacles change the path after takeoff. Watch where the first landing occurs in each run.

en.summary: Face zombie waves in Dead Strike. Learn the controls, use breaks to reload and spend mission rewards on upgrades for later encounters.
en.aboutTitle: Learn how each upgrade changes a wave
about: Dead Strike puts you in ruined urban game maps with waves of zombies. Some enemies reach you more quickly than others. Follow the movement on screen before committing to one target.

Your in-game loadout can change during a mission. Keep track of the current magazine and use a break between waves to reload. Check the selected weapon after switching so the next shot behaves the way you expect.

Mission rewards can buy upgrades to attributes such as reload speed and magazine capacity. Pay attention to where a run gets difficult. If frequent reloads interrupt a wave, compare improvements that address that part of the game.
steps: Move with the keyboard
Use WASD or the arrow keys to reposition your character and keep the approaching wave in view.
Aim and fire with the mouse
Move the pointer to aim at an on-screen zombie, then click to fire the active game weapon.
Reload and switch between waves
Press R to reload and use the mouse wheel to switch the active weapon. Check the new selection before the next group arrives.
Spend a mission reward on one improvement
Compare the listed changes to damage, reload speed or magazine size. Test the upgrade in a familiar mission before spending again.
faq: How do I change weapons?
Scroll the mouse wheel to switch the active in-game weapon.
Which key reloads?
Press R. A break between waves gives you time to complete the reload.
What can mission currency improve?
The game offers upgrades such as damage, accuracy, reload speed and magazine size, as well as equipment unlocks.

en.summary: Click the meme character for points in Goo Goo Gaga Clicker. Buy per-click or automatic upgrades and use temporary bonuses to reach new characters.
en.aboutTitle: Spend points on how you want to earn them
about: Clicking the character earns points for your first upgrades. Some purchases raise the value of each click. Others earn points automatically while the game runs, giving you a different way to reach the next milestone.
The bonus bar rewards active clicking. When it fills, the points from each click double. If a temporary power-up appears, watch its effect before using your balance on a permanent change.

New forms appear as you reach milestones. Try one upgrade and watch your next round of earnings before buying again. Compare points from a short clicking burst with what the automatic upgrades produce when you pause.
steps: Click the character to earn points
Start on the main screen and watch the total after each click. Open the upgrade options when you can afford one.
Pick an active or automatic upgrade
Choose more points per click for an active session. Pick automatic production when you want the total to keep rising between clicks.
Watch the bonus bar
Track the bar while you click. Use the doubled per-click reward while it is active.
Review the next milestone
Check the next upgrade cost after a bonus ends. Save toward a purchase that supports the way you plan to play.
faq: Do I have to click continuously?
Some upgrades produce points automatically while the game runs. Early clicks help you afford the first of those upgrades.
What happens when the bonus bar fills?
It doubles the points earned per click. Watch the bar to see when the bonus ends.
How do new characters appear?
New character forms are unlocked as you reach progression milestones.

en.summary: Flip a bottle across living-room furniture in Bottle Hop. Time single and double jumps, avoid hazards and collect rewards for bottle skins.
en.aboutTitle: Choose the next landing before the bottle takes off
about: Bottle Hop turns shelves, tables and speakers into stepping stones. Click to flip the bottle off its current surface and aim for the next one. Level runs ask you to reach the finish without touching the floor.

A double click gives you an extra jump for larger gaps. Use it when the next surface is beyond the reach of a single flip. On short hops, the extra movement can carry the bottle past an otherwise easy landing.

Later layouts add moving hazards, such as fans and falling objects. Watch the landing area long enough to see whether it stays clear. Endless mode lets you try a longer sequence of flips, and collected gems and caps can unlock more skins.
steps: Click once for a nearby surface
Look at the closest piece of furniture and tap the left mouse button to flip toward it.
Use a double jump for wider gaps
Double-click when a single flip will fall short. Check where the bottle can come down after the extra jump.
Wait for a moving hazard to clear
Watch how a fan or other moving object affects the landing area. Start the jump when there is room to reach the surface.
Practice a short route before Endless
Use level stages to get used to the distance of a single flip. In Endless, apply that timing when the route gives you a narrow platform.
faq: Which input makes the bottle flip?
Use a left click for a single flip. A double click gives you the extra jump.
What happens if the bottle touches the floor?
The level attempt ends. Look for a piece of furniture you can reach with the jump you have available.
What are gems and gold caps for?
They help unlock bottle skins you can use in later runs.

en.summary: Ride a motocross bike over narrow platforms and high ramps. Control your speed and pitch to reach the finish and earn up to three stars.
about: Build enough speed before a wide gap. Once airborne, use forward or backward lean to line up both wheels with the landing.
A checkpoint gives you another shot at a difficult stretch. Use it to compare a slower approach with a more aggressive launch.
steps: Set your speed
Ease off before a narrow landing and accelerate on the approach to wider gaps.
Level the bike
Lean to follow the angle of the landing, then resume accelerating once your wheels touch down.
faq: Why do I crash right after landing?
Check the angle of your bike and the speed you carry onto the platform. A flatter landing gives you more room to correct.

en.summary: Slide through rally checkpoints before the clock runs out and adapt your turns to gravel, asphalt and mud.
about: Survival mode keeps sending you to new checkpoints. Each one adds time, so a steady run matters more than a single long slide.
Challenge stages give you targets such as timed laps or a drift score. Use the surface to choose an entry speed for each turn.
steps: Steer into a turn
Use A and D or the arrow keys. Tap Space for a handbrake turn and straighten before the next checkpoint.
Brake before slippery sections
Use S or the down arrow to slow down. Mud gives you less room to correct after the car starts sliding.
faq: Why does the timer keep running after a checkpoint?
Each checkpoint gives you extra seconds for the next stretch. In Survival, the bonus gets smaller as you advance.

en.summary: Guide a line of wheelbarrows through fields of crops. Sell your harvest and grow the line so you can cover more ground on the next pass.
about: You start with three wheelbarrows. Steer along the outline of each crop pattern first so you can spot any rows you missed.
Longer wheelbarrow lines cover wider strips. Animal helpers can harvest alongside you as you unlock farms with different fields and crops.
steps: Move through the field
Use WASD or the arrow keys. Leave room to turn at the end of a row.
Spend your harvest
Sell crops and increase the size of your wheelbarrow line when repeated passes are slowing you down.
faq: What makes golden crops worth collecting?
Golden crops sell for more than ordinary crops. Make a short detour when one is near your route.

en.summary: Send colour-matched ants to carry away blocks and reveal a 3D pixel-art figure. Plan your moves around five waiting slots.
about: Each ant box goes into one of five slots. Its ants carry away reachable blocks of the same colour until the box is cleared.
White rings mark blocks that ants can reach. Removing those blocks can expose new ones underneath, so check the sculpture after every choice.
steps: Start with an exposed colour
Click an ant box that matches several reachable blocks. Clearing the box makes its slot available again.
Save room for the next colour
Check which blocks a move will uncover before filling the last waiting slot.
faq: What happens if I pick a blocked colour?
The box waits until matching blocks become reachable. The level can jam if all five slots are occupied by colours that cannot move.

en.summary: Compare characters to the target picture, then open surprise boxes and build a collection you can dress up.
about: Matching characters depends on small visual details. Compare faces, colours and accessories before committing to a choice.
Surprise sets add more characters to the collection. Try different clothes and accessories once you have unlocked them.
steps: Look closely at the target
Check the face and outfit first, then compare any small details that distinguish the closest candidates.
Open sets as you progress
Look through the collection after opening a box to see which characters and items are new.
faq: Is matching based only on colour?
No. Similar colours can appear on different characters, so compare the face and accessories as well.

en.summary: Rotate the neon tower so a bouncing ball drops through platform gaps. Chain several drops to trigger Fire Mode and avoid red blocks on ordinary bounces.
about: Each bounce buys a moment to line the tower up with the next opening. Watch the platform below the ball while it is in the air.
Dropping through several gaps in a row can activate Fire Mode. Use that brief window to keep descending through barriers.
steps: Rotate the tower
Drag sideways with the mouse or use the left and right arrow keys to bring a gap under the ball.
Look down the tower
Line up consecutive openings when you can. Check for red blocks before letting the ball fall.
faq: What does Fire Mode do?
A long drop can make the ball smash through platforms for a short time. When it ends, watch for red blocks again.

en.summary: Curve free kicks around a defensive wall and past the goalkeeper. Adjust direction, power and spin as the targets get harder to reach.
about: A straight shot can work with a clear path to goal. If the wall blocks your angle, add spin to bend the ball toward an open corner.
Later stadiums introduce moving defenders and wind. Watch the keeper and pick your target before starting the swipe.
steps: Choose a target
Look for a gap near a post or above the wall, then drag to send the ball toward it.
Adjust the curve
If the ball hits the wall, change your swipe angle or spin on the next attempt. Keep the amount of power similar until the curve works.
faq: Why does the same shot miss in a different stadium?
Wind and moving obstacles can change the shot. Check where the ball is pushed off course and adjust the next swipe.

en.summary: Fire coloured marbles into a moving chain. Match three or more of a colour and clear the track before the chain reaches the skull pit.
about: Close a gap between two groups of the same colour to set up a chain reaction. If the current marble has no useful shot, check the reserve colour.
Filling the progress bar stops new marbles from entering. You still need to clear the chain already on the track to finish the level.
steps: Find a matching group
Aim with the mouse and left-click to fire. A match needs three or more marbles of the same colour.
Use the reserve
Right-click to swap the current and reserve marbles when the other colour gives you a better shot.
faq: Why is the level still going after the bar fills?
The bar stops new arrivals. Remove the marbles already on the track before they reach the end.

en.summary: Stay on the rear wheel as long as you can. Feather the throttle and brake, then try tricks and stars to multiply your score.
about: Holding the gas lifts the front wheel. Too much throttle can tip the bike backward, while braking lowers the front wheel.
Tail scrapes, tricks and stars can multiply the score. Get comfortable balancing a basic wheelie before combining bonuses.
steps: Lift the front wheel
Hold D, Right Arrow or Space to accelerate. Ease off when the front wheel climbs too far.
Correct the angle
Use A or Left Arrow to brake. Once you can hold a steady angle, try W to stand on the seat or S to perform a trick.
faq: Do earned points count after a fall?
Yes, the run ends, but you keep the points and coins earned during the attempt.

en.summary: Restore a family farm, grow crops and turn your harvest into goods for shops and delivery orders.
about: Check the quest list at the car to see which repairs and crops to start with. Crops keep growing while you are away.
Feed animals to collect ingredients for workshops. Truck orders earn coins and experience, and a train station opens larger deliveries later on.
steps: Open the quest list
Interact with the car and follow the early tasks to repair buildings and plant wheat.
Choose a delivery
Check what the truck needs before selling ingredients at the roadside shop. Keep enough for recipes in progress.
faq: Will my fields grow while I am away?
Yes. Come back to harvest, then use crops in workshops or sell them through available orders.
